summary: Revive is a big, engine-building euro where you race across a hex map to claim ancient sites and populate them for points, while managing a growing hand of technology and resource cards through a bag/deck-building layer. Turns involve efficient action selection and long-term tech planning, with almost no direct player interaction beyond racing for the same spots.
praised: Strong table presence with the dual-layer boards and chunky components
Deep, satisfying engine building with meaningful tech tree choices
High variability from randomized ancient sites, tribe powers, and modular setup keeps replays fresh
Solid solo mode and a well-paced 5-scenario campaign that eases players into the rules
Good production value for the price point
criticised: Rulebook and iconography are dense and can be confusing early on
Significant setup and teardown time given the number of components
Some player interaction is limited to racing for the same ancient sites, which can feel too solitaire for groups wanting more conflict
Early turns can feel slow while engines are still being built
Campaign progression means the base game is less interesting once unlocks are exhausted, until you've gone through it

interaction.kind: mostly parallel play with racing/blocking for ancient sites and shared resource spaces

scoring.why: Points come from populated ancient sites, technology advancement, completed objectives, and leftover resources, so the winner is usually whoever built the most efficient overall engine rather than one dominant strategy
